2.  AUTHORIZATION TO SUBMIT APPLICATION FOR GRANT FUNDS UNDER THE
  EDWARD BYRNE MEMORIAL JUSTICE ASSISTANCE GRANT (JAG) AND PUBLIC
  HEARING – F2M5-41, N2M26-117, M2M26-147
  Chief of Police KENNEDY delivered a staff report. The City of Alhambra is eligible for
  $13,276.00 in funds under a federal grant program known as the Edward Byrne Memorial
  Justice Assistance Grant (JAG). The formula used to determine this amount was based
  upon a minimum base allocation, population, and major crime statistics.

  The 2026 JAG funds would be used to acquire software, personal protective equipment
  for sworn personnel, and specialized tools that support officer safety and critical incident
  response. The grant guidelines required the City conduct a public hearing to receive
  community input concerning the use of funds, and approval of the application and pertinent
  requirements. Once the City Council designates the Police Chief as the JAG Grant
  Administrator, the Police Chief or his Designee would be responsible for the expenditure
  of funds, monitoring the award, and submitting the required reports.

  Open Public Hearing:  Mayor Andrade-Stadler opened the public hearing.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCammon spoke in favor of the item.

  Close Public Hearing:  After receiving public comment, Mayor Andrade-Stadler
  closed the public hearing.

  Discussion:  Councilmember LEE discussed the amount of the grant and
  the need for additional grant funding. City Manager BINNQUIST and Chief KENNEDY
  provided clarification as to the City’s grant process and research into new grants.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized staff to apply for grant funds to acquire
  software, personal protective equipment for sworn personnel, and specialized tools that
  support officer safety and critical incident response under the United States Department
  of Justice, Bureau of Justice Assistance, Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance
  Grant (JAG); conducted a public hearing regarding use of the funds as required by the
  grant; appropriated expenditure and revenue funds in the amount of $13,276.00 in Fiscal
  Year 2026-27; designated the Chief of Police or Designee as the JAG Grant Administrator;
  and directed staff undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s actions. (M2M26-
  147)

  Vote:  Moved:  MAZA  Seconded:  WANG
  Ayes:  LEE, MALONEY, WANG, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

3.  RESOLUTION ESTABLISHING THE HELLMAN AVENUE  NEIGHBORHOOD
  PREFERRED PARKING DISTRICT- F2M26-7, F2M26-44
  Management Analyst ALVAREZ delivered the presentation. On May 11, 2026, during
  public comment, numerous residents expressed concern about spillover parking
  associated with the nearby Courtyard by Marriott. During Council Communications,
  Councilmember Wang requested an item to discuss parking concerns and a Preferred
  Parking District (PPD) at the next City Council meeting.

  On June 22, 2026, Council directed staff to undertake community outreach in order to
  determine potential PPD boundaries and applicable days/times.

  On August 5, 2026, a community survey was distributed to residents on West Hellman
  Avenue, South Curtis Avenue, South Olive Avenue, and Hathaway Avenue. The survey
  requested feedback on potential PPD boundaries, as well as preferred days and times for
  parking enforcement. The survey was distributed to 93 households, of which 20
  responded, representing approximately 22% of the total households within the proposed
  PPD. Of the 20 respondents, 15 were in favor of establishing a PPD, detailed in
  Attachment 1. Of those 15 respondents, 43% were in favor of establishing a two-hour
  parking accommodation for guests and service providers.

  Public Comment:
  1) Caleb Kwok spoke against the PPD and expressed concerns regarding the broad
  parking restrictions.

  2) Lewis McCammon discussed the item and supported staff’s efforts to address the
  concerns of residents.

  3) Bruce Mok spoke in support of the PPD and thanked the City for quickly addressing
  residents’ concerns. He suggested staff work with the City of Monterey Park regarding
  their street sweeping restrictions.

  Discussion:  Councilmember WANG supported the Resolution and requested
  staff continue to monitor the situation. Ms. WANG and City Manager BINNQUIST
  discussed the PPD and the restrictions. Ms. BINNQUIST clarified that staff would review
  the Alhambra Municipal code sections pertaining to PPD and would be making changes
  for additional guest passes. Ms. BINNQUIST also provided further clarification as to the
  process to implement the PPD and the public notification. Ms. WANG reported that in
  addition to staff outreach, she also canvassed the area to provide more information to
  residents. She requested that as the city moves into the implementation phase, that the
  City allow for a 2-week grace period to provide additional warnings and information to
  residents. She also requested additional outreach on site in the PPD with staff present at
  a hyper-local pop-up event.

  Councilmember MALONEY supported the Resolution and Ms. Wang’s suggestion for
  additional outreach. Councilmember LEE supported Ms. Wang’s suggestion for additional
  outreach and continued to discuss language barriers in the community. Ms. LEE further
  suggested Ms. Wang meet with Ms. Binnquist to continue to discuss the public outreach
  efforts. Vice Mayor MAZA supported Ms. Wang’s suggestions. Mayor ANDRADE-

September 28, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting  Page 4 of 12
   STADLER agreed with the additional outreach for the PPD.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved Resolution R2M26-27 establishing a
  Preferred Parking District (PPD) in the Hellman Avenue neighborhood adjacent to the
  Courtyard by Marriott, directed that the PPD would go into effect after a 2-week grace
  period beginning when signage has been installed, directed staff to provide hyper-local
  community outreach with a pop-up event at Hellman Avenue and Hathaway intersection,
  and directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  WANG  Seconded:  MALONEY
  Ayes:  LEE, MALONEY, WANG, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

4.  FISCAL YEAR 2025/26 TO FISCAL YEAR 2026/27 CARRYOVERS. – F2M25-17,
  F2M26-17, R2M26-28
  In June 2026, the City Council amended the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Budget, which allocated
  funds to the various Departments and accounts within each of the City’s operating funds.
  As part of the year-end financial review, the Departments identified certain unexpended
  and unencumbered appropriations that remain necessary for ongoing projects and
  operations. These appropriations were proposed to be carried forward into Fiscal Year
  2026/27 and are detailed in Exhibit I.

  At the close of Fiscal Year 2025/26, there were outstanding encumbrances representing
  valid contracts and/or purchase orders for goods and services that were ordered but not
  received as of June 30, 2026. These encumbrances remained unexpended and were
  recommended for reappropriation into Fiscal Year 2026/27 and are detailed in Exhibit II.
  The City Manager and Director of Finance reviewed each request and recommend
  approval of the requests of encumbrances and carryovers identified in Exhibit I and
  subsequently, the budget adjustments in Exhibit II.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved Resolution No. R2M26-28 approving Fiscal
  Year-end carryovers from Fiscal Year 2025/26 to Fiscal Year 2026/27 and the
  reappropriation of outstanding encumbrances as of the close of Fiscal Year 2025/26, and
  directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action.

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  WANG
  Ayes:  LEE, MALONEY, WANG, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

 5.  APPROVING THE APPLICATION OF GRANT FUNDS UNDER THE INTEGRATED
  CLIMATE ADAPTATION AND RESILIENCY PROGRAM (ICARP) FOR THE CREATION
  OF AN URBAN FORESTRY MANAGEMENT PLAN AND THE PLANTING OF TREES
  CITYWIDE– F2M26-18, M2M26-149
  A total of $27.5 million was available for funding heat related projects from the California
  Climate Bond (Proposition 4) and State’s Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund. The proposed
  grant application was in direct alignment with the City’s Sustainability Plan’s Green Space
  Goal of increasing the City’s tree canopy.

  Staff was in the process of preparing an ICARP grant application to fund the development
  of the City’s first Urban Forestry Management Plan (UFMP). A UFMP would be beneficial
  to the City by recommending types of species to plant and identifying where the need to
  increase the canopy was the greatest. The focus of the selection of trees would be native
  drought-tolerant species. Ongoing, the document would serve to advise City staff on how
  to maintain a healthy urban forest. In addition, grant funds would be used for planting trees
  and providing public outreach on the benefits trees have on society. The funding request
  of $750,000 was based on estimates to produce the UFMP and the planting of trees along
  with maintenance to continue through the establishment period. A requirement of the grant
  application was to identify at least one Co-Applicant that would serve as a partner
  throughout the project from application through completion. The partnership was meant to
  strengthen the project by pairing municipal agencies with community-based organizations
  with subject matter expertise. Staff identified TreePeople and Active San Gabriel Valley
  (ActiveSGV) as Co-Applicant partners on this project application. TreePeople is a
  community-based organization that has for the past fifty years planted and cared for
  millions of trees, restored thousands of acres of fire-scarred wildlands, and helped educate
  hundreds of thousands of environmentalists. As technical advisors, TreePeople would be
  assigned to produce the UFMP.ActiveSGV is a San Gabriel Valley-based nonprofit that
  works with communities to create healthier, more equitable neighborhoods through active
  transportation, environmental justice, and community-led projects. ActiveSGV would work
  with City staff to provide the public outreach, a critical component to the success of this
  project.

  After Council review and discussion of the proposed ICARP grant application at the
  September 14, 2026 City Council meeting, the Council requested additional information
  regarding the scope of work and related costs from the co-applicants. The proposal by
  TreePeople for the creation of the City’s First Urban Forestry Management Plan (UFMP)
  and to serve as serve as an advisor on the City’s tree planting project was for an estimated
  $428,013.44. The proposal submitted by ActiveSGV for public outreach is for an estimated
  $191,970. The outreach would consist of various proposed methods including twelve
  community tabling events, four community canvasing events and a survey to assist the
  City in reaching the public both on the Urban Forestry Management Plan and the
  distribution of trees. The remaining balance would be $130,016.44. Those funds would be
  spent on purchasing additional trees, where demand and available planting space was
  warranted, and $25,000 would be set aside as required by the grant for post-award
  activities.

September 28, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting  Page 6 of 12
   Staff requested the Council authorize the partnerships with TreePeople and ActiveSGV to
  execute the City’s tree planning and planting efforts as it relates to the ICARP grant.

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCammon spoke in support of the Grant and discussed the
  item.

  Discussion:  Councilmember WANG spoke in support of the item and went on to
  discuss the scope of work and suggested the City continue to add trees to the City. She
  also discussed the maintenance of existing trees and City Manager BINNQUIST provided
  clarification regarding the Urban Forestry Management Plan. Ms. WANG also discussed
  the timeline of the project with Grants Specialist TABER. Ms. WANG requested updates
  be provided to Council at each milestone of the project timeline.

  Councilmember LEE also expressed her concerns regarding tree maintenance as aging
  trees affect sidewalks and lose branches. She suggested part of the grant be set aside for
  ongoing tree maintenance for existing trees. Ms. BINNQUIST provided clarification and
  requested Council provide consensus as to the use of funds for maintenance or planting
  new trees. Ms. LEE requested that staff continue to provide outreach to residents and
  business owners as to the location and type of trees planted.

  Councilmember MALONEY spoke in support of the item and further discussed the ways
  the item supported the city’s ongoing goals for functional green space, environmental
  sustainability, and the need to plant more trees.

  Mayor ANDRADE-STADLER spoke in support of the item and noted that there should be
  equitable distribution throughout the five districts.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved the City’s application titled, “Let’s Grow
  Alhambra, A Tree Forward Approach to Combating Extreme Heat” to the Integrated
  Climate Adaptation and Resiliency Program (ICARP) to fund the City’s first Urban Forestry
  Management Plan and the planting of trees; authorized the designation of TreePeople and
  Active San Gabriel Valley (ActiveSGV) as grant co-applicants; authorized the City
  Manager, or designee, to execute all grant documents; and directed staff to undertake the
  steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action (M2M26-149)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  WANG
  Ayes:  LEE, MALONEY, WANG, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER
  Noes:  NONE
  Absent:  NONE

6.  TREASURER’S REPORT AS OF AUGUST 31, 2026 – F2M26-1

  adopted by the City Council on June 22, 2026. The August 2026 Treasurer’s Report listed
  investments held by the City as of August 31, 2026 as well as the current market value for
  such investments. All investments were made in accordance with the City’s Investment
  Policy Statement as adopted by the City Council. The City invested primarily in the State
  of California’s Local Agency Investment Fund, Certificates of Deposit and U.S.
  Government Treasury and U.S. Agency securities, all of which were considered safe
  investments. Investments were also considered for liquidity and yield. Securities were
  purchased to be held until maturity and not to be traded for short term gains; however, if

7.  NOTICE OF COMPLETION - FRONT STREET WATER MAIN REPLACEMENT AND
  ZONE CHANGE - PHASE 2– F2M19-20, N2M24-150, C2M25-10, M2M26-150

  On March 24, 2025, the City Council awarded Contract C2M25-10 to Stephen Doreck
  Equipment Rentals Inc, for the Front Street Water Main Replacement and Zone Change -
  Phase 2 in the amount of $2,263,102.00.

  There were three authorized change orders during the project for the installation of an 18-
  inch line stop to tie-in the new water main pipe on Marengo Avenue, for concrete pavement
  on Cherry Lane, and for an 8-inch gate valve and 16 additional water service lines. Various
  miscellaneous items were also credited to the City. The change orders decreased the total
  contract amount by $188,155.25, resulting in a final project amount of $2,074,946.75.

  The project was completed in accordance with the City’s requirements and specifications.
  As such, it was appropriate for the City Council to accept the project as complete and
  instruct the City Clerk that the Notice of Completion be filed with the County of Los Angeles
  Recorder’s Office.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council accepted the work of Stephen Doreck Equipment
  Rentals Inc, for the Front Street Water Main Replacement and Zone Change - Phase 2 in
  the amount of $2,074,946.75 as complete; directed the City Clerk to file a Notice of
  Completion with the County of Los Angeles for recordation; released the five percent
  retention 35 days from the date of recordation, if no liens are filed; and directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize Council’s action (M2M26-150)

8.  AMENDMENT OF CONTRACT WITH STARCHASE GPS SOLUTIONS FOR POLICE
  PURSUIT MITIGATION TECHNOLOGY– F2M23-69, C2M23-84, M2M26-151

  The Alhambra Police Department has continued to seek strategies and acquire technology
  to mitigate crime and safely apprehend criminal offenders. In 2024, Alhambra Police were
  involved in 29 pursuits; 30 pursuits in 2025, and 21 in 2026 (year-to-date). Such vehicle

September 28, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting  Page 8 of 12
   pursuits pose substantial safety risks to the community and law enforcement; in addition,
  in certain instances, fleeing suspects might never get identified, apprehended, or
  criminally prosecuted.

  In October 2023, the City approved a contract with StarChase GPS Solutions to provide
  a law enforcement tool (vehicle mounted/installed and hand-held device) that would allow
  a Police Officer to tag and track a suspect vehicle from a distance prior to or during a
  vehicle pursuit.

  The initial contract was for three years, with a one-time upfront payment of $89,741.24.
  This contract was set to expire in October 2026.

  The StarChase GPS law enforcement tool has been successfully deployed approximately
  two dozen times since its inception at the Alhambra Police Department and has aided
  police officers with safely apprehending suspects wanted for grand theft auto, evading,
  robbery, drug sales, and other crimes. A contract renewal would allow Alhambra Police to
  continue equipping its officers with this law enforcement tool

  Public Comment:  Lewis McCammon discussed the item as presented, previous
  incidents of fatal police pursuits, and the need for safety measures for police and public.
  He supported the item.

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council amended a contract with StarChase GPS Solutions to
  include a three (3) year, seven (7) month subscription renewal in the amount of $32,833.52
  for a total amount not to exceed $122,574.76, subject to final language approval by the
  City Manager and City Attorney; authorized the Chief of Police to execute said contract;
  and directed staff to undertake the steps necessary to finalize the City Council’s action.
  (M2M26-151)

  Vote:  Moved:  MALONEY  Seconded:  ANDRADE-STADLER
  Ayes:  LEE, MALONEY, WANG, MAZA, ANDRADE-STADLER

10.  AUTHORIZE A TRANSFER OF FUNDS FROM THE CAPITAL OUTLAY FUND TO THE
  GENERAL FUND FOR THE PURCHASE OF APPLE IPAD PRO EQUIPMENT FOR
  FIRE AND EMERGENCY MEDICAL DISPATCHING – F2M5-70, F2M26-25, M2M26-148

  The City of Alhambra has contracted with Verdugo Cities for fire and emergency medical
  dispatching services since 2005. As part of the new computer aided dispatch (CAD)
  system, agencies were required to upgrade their mobile data terminals from a PC based
  system to iOS Tablet System utilizing Apple iPad Pro equipment. The upgrades also
  required a new mount/docking station. Per the Verdugo agreement, the cost of the
  equipment is the responsibility of the contracting agency. Verdugo procures and installs
  the necessary equipment. The Alhambra Fire Department’s costs would be $30,115.99

  Discussion:  None.

  Action Taken:  City Council authorized a transfer of funds from the Capital Outlay

  emergency medical dispatching in the amount of $30,115.99; and directed staff to
  undertake the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action (M2M26-148)

11.  AUTHORIZE A PARTICIPATION AGREEMENT WITH SOCALREN FOR
  STREAMLINED SAVINGS PATHWAY DIRECT INSTALL PROGRAM TO UPGRADE
  WATER HEATERS AT CITY FACILITIES – F2M26-18, M2M26-152

  The Southern California Regional Energy Network (SoCalREN) is authorized by the
  California Public Utilities Commission to deliver energy efficiency programs to local
  communities. Its Streamlined Savings Pathway Direct Install Program assists public
  agencies with equipment and system upgrades at low- or no-cost to the participating
  agency. SoCalREN provides end-to-end support, from identifying equipment upgrades to
  coordinating low- or no-cost installation by a qualified contractor. As a member of
  SoCalREN, the City was eligible for this program.

September 28, 2026 Regular City Council Meeting  Page 10 of 12
   SoCalREN offered incentives to public agencies to upgrade existing water heaters to high-
  efficiency tankless water heaters or heat pump water heaters. Staff identified several City
  facilities needing water heater replacement and/or upgrade that would be good candidates
  for this program. Potential projects for SoCalREN’s consideration might include water
  heater upgrades at Police and Fire stations, Park & Recreation facilities, City Hall, the City
  Yard, and the Library. Replacing existing, aging water heaters with tankless or heat pump
  water heaters would improve energy efficiency and conserve water at these City
  properties.

  City Council approval was needed to participate in the program and enter into the
  participation agreement with SoCalREN. Projects completed through this program support
  the City’s sustainability goals to increase energy efficiency and water conservation in
  municipal buildings and operations.

  Action Taken:  City Council approved a Public Agency Participation Agreement,
  subject to final language approval by the City Manager and City Attorney, with the
  Southern California Regional Energy Network for the Streamlined Savings Pathway Direct
  Install Program to upgrade water heaters at City facilities; authorized the City Manager, or
  designee, to sign the agreement and related documents; and directed staff to undertake
  the steps necessary to finalize the Council’s action. (M2M26-152)
